newsitem.title: GERMANY: German farmers oppose Santer's EU reform plans.
newsitem.headline: German farmers oppose Santer's EU reform plans.

text.p: German farm union (DBV) president Gerd Sonnleitner rejected price-cutting farm reform plans presented by European Commission President Jacques Santer earlier on Wednesday.
"Strategic thinking ahead of new world trade rounds and eastwards expansion of the EU is necessary," he said in a statement on the proposals, known as Agenda 2000.
"But equally important are long-term perspectives for our farmers and their participation in the general income growth."
DBV was ready to discuss the package constructively, but it would not shy away from a tough confrontation if necessary, Sonnleitner said.
German farmers stood to lose one fifth of their incomes from beef, grain, oilseeds and milk if the proposals were implemented.
An envisaged shift to direct payments to farmers, rather than aid based on certain crops, would create more bureaucracy and, via new area ceilings, bring more injustice in the division of aid.
It was also unfair that the farm budget should bear the brunt of the cost of the political EU goal to integrate eastern Europe.
The EU's bargaining position in the next round of World Trade Organisation (WTO) talks would be weakened if negotiators made voluntary price cuts ahead of the talks.
But Sonnleitner agreed with the EU plan to extend milk quotas at their current levels until 2006.

Farm co-op organisation DRV said planned cuts in cereals intervention prices, outlined in the proposal, could threaten production of high quality grains in Germany. The merging of separate area aid into one premium would threaten current oilseed output levels, both for food and feeds as well as for industrial crops.
